chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorced his wife, then left her until her waiting period ended, then married her again, then divorced her without having intercourse with her, and he did this three times, he said: 'She is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife three times without intercourse each time?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the specific mechanism of 'Tanzil al-Talaq' (divorce without consummation), establishing that three such divorces trigger the major prohibition (Nikah al-Mu'addah). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the wife must marry a new husband, consummate that union, and then be divorced or widowed before she can return to her first husband, a process known as 'Tahil'.
